newsitem.title: USA: Dow sets first record close for New Year.
newsitem.headline: Dow sets first record close for New Year.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average racked up its first record close for the New Year Monday, building on the momentum that produced 44 record finishes in 1996.

The Dow rose 23.09 points to close at 6,567.18, surpassing the record of 6,560.91 set on Dec. 27. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,396 to 1,110 on active volume of 527 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq index also set a record, rising 5.72 points to 1,316.40.
Despite the records for the major stock indices, Wall Street's overall performance was mixed, with broad indicators exhibiting little of the momentum showed by blue chips.
Even the 30-stock Dow index, which raced up nearly 75 points in early trading was well off its peak level, pulled down by a series of computer selling programmes in late trade.
The strength in stocks was concentrated among economically-sensitive companies, which benefited from a growing perception that the economy was still expanding at a solid pace.
"There's no question that the recent numbers have continued to run on the strong side," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter.
"Housing, construction and consumer confidence have all been strong," he said. "The first implication of all that is just better earnings."
The earnings argument that propelled the Dow to a 101.60-point gain last Friday, held sway for most of the session, fuelling a rally.
Even as stocks were rising, however, fear that economic growth could also bring higher inflation ate away at the bond market, where interest rates crept steadily higher all day.
Eventually, analysts said, that concern spread to the stock market.

"If rates are trending higher, you don't buy bank stocks and bank stocks were weak today," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "That shows the thought of higher rates was creeping into investment decisions."
Among economically sensitive stocks, General Motors Corp. added 1-3/8 to 59-1/4. Smith Barney upgraded the shares of the giant carmaker and raised its 1997 earnings estimate.
Stocks of oil companies also were strong as cold weather across the United States drove domestic crude prices above $26 per barrel.
February crude oil soared 78 cents to end at $26.37 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange, nearing its six-year high of $26.80 set in late December of last year.
Texaco Inc. rose 1-3/8 to 102 and Exxon Corp. gained 1-3/8 to 100.
Toys R Us tumbled 4-5/8 to 26-1/8 after the company said its holiday sales were disappointing.

Apple Computer Corp. skidded 3-7/8 to 17-7/8 in reaction to its statement late Friday that its fiscal first quarter loss would far exceed analysts' expectations. Several brokerage houses downgraded Apple's shares, and expressed doubts about the firm's ability to revive its business soon.
Bank stocks were mostly lower, pressured by the weaker bond market and rising interest rates.
Chase Manhattan Corp. fell 7/8 to 87-3/8, Citicorp fell 3/4 to 103-3/4 and First Union Corp eased 5/8 to 74.
The bellwether 30-year Treasury was down half a point, or $5 per $1,000 face value, bumping up its yield to 6.77 percent from 6.73 percent at Friday's close.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 0.38 of a point to 747.65. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.39 to 572.06.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.22 to 394.28. The average share was up 2 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,253.436 up 10.154 or 0.14 percent.
